# Legacy role-name authorization sites — what REMAINS after Phase 4.
#
# Generated by `case_service/hxguard/legacy_sites.py::scan()` and compared
# against a live scan by tests/phase_authz. A line here is a router function
# that still reads the identity model.
#
# Phase 4 step 2 (2026-08-15) took this list from 205 sites to 75.
# What is left is deliberate, and falls into four kinds. NONE of them is a
# role-name authorization decision:
#
#   1. `superadmin` identity tests — the permanent break-glass bypass
#      (design §2.3). `"superadmin" in user.roles`, usually to skip tenant
#      scoping. Never migrating; superadmin is an identity, not a privilege.
#   2. Display and serialization — `_user_dict`, `_to_response`, `_make_tokens`
#      put `roles` into a response or a token. They decide nothing.
#   3. Literal role membership where role-INHERITANCE was the bug —
#      `hxdbmanager._is_service_account` matches "service" exactly, because
#      `has_role("service")` classified every admin as a service account and
#      silently disabled that endpoint's per-user rate limit.
#   4. `has_privilege(...)` on the CASE-LEVEL vocabulary (`case_type`,
#      `db_manager`) — access-group privileges, which is the model Phase 4
#      migrates *toward*. Step 3 removed this call's fallback to `is_admin`.
#
# The detector cannot tell these apart from a real decision — it reads the
# identity model, which is all four of these too — so the ledger is what
# separates them. To add a genuinely new authorization decision, add an
# hxguard action; do not add a line here.
#
# Recorded 2026-08-15 (Phase 4). Was 205 sites / 24 routers at Phase 3.5.
# Now 75 sites / 13 routers (55 endpoints, 20 helpers).
#
# 2026-08-16 — omnichannel added eight `channels.py` sites, all kind 1: the
# agent surfaces read `"superadmin" in user.roles` to decide whether to apply
# tenant scoping, exactly as `access_groups.py` and `user_directory.py` already
# do. Authorization for those routes is `hxguard.guard("channels.*")`.
#
# 2026-08-16 — enterprise identity P2 added five `scim.py` sites, all kind 1.
# Every SCIM route reads `is_superadmin` to refuse managing that account: the
# superadmin exists so a human can recover the platform, and an external
# directory that could see or change it would make that recovery path the
# directory administrator's to take away. Authorization for these routes is the
# `scim_principal` bearer-token dependency, not a role name.
#
# 2026-08-17 — `identity_admin.py::list_account_links` was missing from this
# ledger since the account-linking screen shipped: it filters
# `is_superadmin.is_(False)` so the superadmin can never be listed as a
# linkable account, which is kind 1. The scan has been red since that commit;
# nothing about it was caused by the SP-key work that found it.
# 2026-09-17 — `retry_index_job` joins `cancel_index_job`: the same
# `_assert_case_access` gate, transitive, for the same reason.
# 2026-09-10 — the document index queue added two `hxnexus.py` sites,
# `list_index_jobs` and `cancel_index_job`, and the same day's audit added a
# third, `upload_and_index`: that route had NO case check at all, so anyone
# signed in could index text into any case's AI context. Giving it the check is
# what put it on this list. Neither reads the identity model
# itself: both call `_assert_case_access`, which is already on this list, and
# the ledger's scan is transitive on purpose. Their authorization is that
# helper — the tenant boundary first, then the case relationship — which is
# exactly what the four hxnexus routes above it use. Recorded rather than
# migrated for the same reason those four were.

# 2026-09-29 (8d): `_assert_role_grant` — only a superadmin grants superadmin
# (break-glass, kind 1). realtime `__init__`/`get_presence` carry roles into
# a socket caller solely for `is_superadmin`.

# 2026-10-19: realtime `websocket_endpoint` — the socket now signs in through
# get_current_user and builds that same socket caller from the checked user
# (kind 1, as `get_presence`); it replaced `_socket_caller`, which read the
# raw claims.
